dish: House-made spaghetti and wood-fired pizza (arancini, mortadella-pistachio pie)
w: The signature restaurant of Cussewago Square, the reborn Meadville distillery/lumber-yard complex built on 1890s cattle pens; high-end scratch Italian with fresh handmade pasta, wood-fired pizza and artisan ingredients in a speakeasy-styled room.

dish: Handcrafted ales and wood-fired pizza brewed over a glass brewhouse floor
w: A family-owned Meadville brewpub open since 2012, brewing on a 10-barrel system visible beneath a glass floor and pairing pub favorites and wood-fired pizza with elegant entrees; grew to a second location in Grove City.

dish: Char-grilled steaks and Italian pasta with regional craft beer in the college town's oldest tavern
w: Edinboro's oldest eating-and-drinking establishment and a turn-of-the-century landmark serving its current purpose since 1952 — a classic neighborhood college-town bar with a strong steak-and-pasta kitchen and a deep list of regional craft beers.

dish: Sugar Moon Maple Amber and Maple Porter brewed with the family's own Howles maple syrup
w: Opened 2019 in a refurbished 19th-century barn along French Creek on the grounds of the lost Riverside Inn, this farm-to-table brewpub is an outgrowth of the four-generation Howles Maple Farm and folds its own maple into beer and food; live music and outdoor summer series.

dish: Hand-dipped chocolate-covered raspberries and small-batch meltaways
w: A downtown Edinboro chocolatier opened in 2019 by the family behind Butler's long-running Peter's Chocolate Shoppe; small-batch fillings made on site, hand-dipped nuts and clusters, and chocolate-covered raspberries, strawberries and Granny Smith apples.

dish: Charcoal-grilled prime rib and hand-cut steaks
w: A lodge-like Mercer County institution since 1979 (the first Springfield Restaurant Group property) right off I-79/I-80 — famous for prime rib and hand-cut steaks over a charcoal grill, a moose head over the bar and a big Sunday brunch; a classic corridor stop.

dish: Small-batch ales poured in a wooded outdoor beer-garden amphitheater
address: 2158 Mercer Butler Pike, Grove City, PA 16127
w: Opened 2019 on wooded property a mile off I-79, Big Rail began as an outdoor beer garden and added a taproom in 2024; a natural amphitheater and stage make it as much a live-music venue as a brewery, named for the heavy rail forged for Pennsylvania's ore and coal trade.

dish: Ingredient-driven handmade pasta sourced almost entirely from Butler County farms
w: Zelienople native chef Rich Burns runs this trattoria-style room in a restored 1940 Mellon Bank, cooking a minimalist, ingredient-driven Italian menu ('nothing more than three or four ingredients') built on a standing relationship with local farmers; a Pittsburgh Magazine favorite.

dish: Scratch-made New American plates and brick-oven pizza from five-star chef Pamela Delaude
w: A Cranberry golf-simulator lounge that hired executive chef Pamela Delaude to give it a country-club-caliber, made-from-scratch New American menu with strong gluten-free options and well-regarded brick-oven pizza; the name nods to 'the turn' between a round's front and back nine.

dish: Small-batch handcrafted ales with from-scratch pizza and BBQ
w: Opened 2013 by Zachary and Erika Shumaker, ShuBrew's Main Street Zelienople brewpub pours small-batch ales (now brewed five minutes away in Harmony) alongside a scratch food menu of pizzas, sandwiches, BBQ and Asian plates with locally sourced proteins.
